newsitem.title: FINLAND: OUTOKUMPU SEES ZINC PRICE RISE IN 1997.
newsitem.headline: OUTOKUMPU SEES ZINC PRICE RISE IN 1997.

text.p: Finnish metals group Outokumpu Oy's chief economist Michael Cook said on Tuesday he expects zinc prices to start rising later this year as stocks would fall amid slow growth in production.
He told a briefing that he forecast a modest upside in nickel prices, but said copper prices would come under pressure as the market starts moving into a surplus next year.

Cook forecast zinc consumption -- about 50 percent of zinc is used for galvanizing steel and some 60 percent of end-users are in the automotive and construction industry -- would grow by 2.5 to 3.0 percent per year this year and next, while a lack of raw materials at smelters would dent output growth.
Zinc stocks would fall below the equivalent of six weeks' need by end 1997 and well below five in 1998, he said.
"That provides a heck of a good basis for higher prices," Cook said.
On Tuesday, zinc traded at $1,233 per tonne on the London metal exchange, corresponding to $0.56 per pound.

A sensitivity analysis printed in Outokumpu's annual report shows a sustained 10 percent rise in the price of zinc from the $0.46 per pound average in 1996 would boost group earnings by 95 million markka.
Cook forecast nickel consumption -- some 70 percent of Nickel is used for stainless steel production -- would rebound by some four to five percent this year and "probably a little less next year".
Production would more or less match this year's growth and accelerate in 1998.
"We predict only small market deficits, by our reckoning stocks will not come down enough to do anything interesting to the price," Cook said adding that stocks may fall to about 10 weeks in 1998.
"It's a recipe for prices to get a little better, we doubt there will be anything exciting," he said.
On Tuesday, nickel cash outrights traded at $7,280 per tonne which corresponds to $3.30 per pound.
A 10 percent sustained deviation either way from last year's $3.40 per pound average nickel price would have a 75 million markka impact on Outokumpu's earnings, Outokumpu says.
Copper prices -- which have been strong recently as a correction to low stocks has been delayed until next year -- would get under pressure, Cook said.

Annual consumption growth would be two to three percent this year and next, but production growth "is gradually overtaking consumption", he said. "Next year the market will move into surplus ... the stock ratio will start rising and that ought to mean lower prices."
But the level of Chinese buying would determine the market and "that is very difficult to predict", he added.

A 10 percent sustained deviation from last year's $1.04 per pound average price for copper would have an 80 million markka impact on Outokumpu's results. On Tuesday, cash copper traded at $2,393 per tonne, corresponding to $1.08 per pound.
Last year, Outokumpu posted a 229 million markka profit before extraordinary items.

Outkumpu's senstivity analysis shows that a 10 percent sustained deviation from last year's 4.5905 average dollar rate against the markka would boost Outokumpu's profit by 350 million markka, all other things equal.
That 10 percent limit is 5.05 for USD/FIM.
USD/FIM on Tuesday traded at 5.1573 per dollar -- 12 percent above the 1996 average -- and it has been above 5.00 most of the year and even above 5.05 frequently.
